title: Restriction-zero sections are killed by a power of an invertible section
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] (the intersection of any two affine opens is quasi-compact), $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $X_s=\{x\in X:s(x)\ne0\text{ in }\mathcal L_x\otimes\kappa(x)\}$, where $\kappa(x)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. If $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ restricts to zero on $X_s$, then there exists $m\ge0$ such that the image of $t$ under multiplication by $s^{\otimes m}$ is zero in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW (label lemma-invert-s-sections), injectivity of the canonical localization map

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_r$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, with $\mathcal L|_{U_i}\cong\mathcal O_{U_i}$; this is possible because $\mathcal L$ is locally free of rank one and $X$ is quasi-compact. Write $s|_{U_i}=f_ie_i$ with $e_i$ a basis of $\mathcal L|_{U_i}$ and $f_i\in R_i$. For $x\in U_i$, $s(x)\ne0$ in $\mathcal L_x\otimes\kappa(x)$ iff the image of $f_i$ in $\kappa(x)$ is nonzero, i.e. iff $f_i\notin\mathfrak p_x$; hence $X_s\cap U_i=D(f_i)$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW, proof of injectivity on a finite affine trivializing cover

proof.text: Since $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ is quasi-coherent, the counit $\widetilde{M_i}\to\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ with $M_i=\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism, and under it the restriction $\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(D(f_i),\mathcal F)$ is the localization map $M_i\to(M_i)_{f_i}$. Since $D(f_i)\subseteq X_s$ and $t|_{X_s}=0$, the element $m_i=t|_{U_i}\in M_i$ satisfies $m_i/1=0$ in $(M_i)_{f_i}$. By the kernel criterion for localization, $um_i=0$ for some $u$ in the powers of $f_i$, so $f_i^{n_i}m_i=0$ for some $n_i\ge0$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW, injectivity calculation after trivializing L on an affine open

proof.text: Because the cover is finite, put $m=\max_in_i$. On $U_i$ we have $s^{\otimes m}|_{U_i}=f_i^me_i^{\otimes m}$, so the image of $t$ under multiplication by $s^{\otimes m}$ restricts on $U_i$ to $f_i^mm_i\otimes e_i^{\otimes m}=0$. As the $U_i$ cover $X$, the sheaf property gives that this image is zero in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW, conclusion of injectivity proof
